body:
Earlier today we had our regular triage meeting, notes are below.  We will skip two weeks of meetings due to the holidays, so next meeting will be January 8th.  That meeting agenda is at #12034.

Notes from the meeting:

- **Canvas Text Writing Mode Update** [#11449](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11449) Stephen Chenney provided an update on the canvas text writing mode. They have finally started work, sent out the standards positions requests a couple of days ago, have an explainer up, and have started on the Chrome implementation. Stephen requested that folks look at their standards-positions and update those, and he work on the spec text after getting the implementation and tests in place.
- **Module Preload for Style and JSON** [#11981](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11981) Kurt Catti-Schmidt discussed the PR for allowing style and JSON as an attribute for module preload. A key issue is whether to remove JSON from standard preload and only allow it in module preload, as JSON is only really usable in a module context, unlike style. Noam Rosenthal agreed that disallowing preload for JSON for standard preload would be better for users by avoiding wasted bandwidth on something that won't be useful. Kurt Catti-Schmidt confirmed this approach was generally agreed upon but noted that the tricky part is how to word the exclusion without creating a "weird special case" in the spec. Olli Pettay expressed concern that the special case wording might be an editorial issue that could cause problems later. Noam Rosenthal suggested using the existing `translate a preload destination` concept within the HTML spec, which is already a closed list that does not allow JSON, simplifying the wording needed for module preload. Kurt Catti-Schmidt will return to the original wording if this approach works and Noam Rosenthal confirmed they would review the comment to clarify the necessary changes. Kurt Catti-Schmidt will be out for the next two weeks.
- **Out-of-Order HTML Streaming Patching** #[11542](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11542) Philip Jägenstedt and Noam Rosenthal provided an update on out-of-order HTML streaming patching, noting that they simplified the methods to only keep `append` and `replace children` in the PR, with other use cases potentially handled by Noam Rosenthal's proposed marker node proposal. The main discussion centered on naming and how to handle interleaved patching, such as continuously updating different parts of the page, which requires both replacing children initially and then continuously appending. Philip reviewed several alternatives for the content method attribute, including an automatic boolean attribute that would replace children first and then append. Olli Pettay found the automatic approach to be potentially confusing. They also discussed using marker nodes, noting that some marker-based options were either too intricate and verbose, requiring a pileup of markers, or involved replacing one marker each time, but still required inserting new markers and led to more combinations for replacement start and end points. Philip Jägenstedt stated that the current PR retains the `content method` with `replace children` and `append`, which still feels like the better trade-off. Olli Pettay found the last option, using a single marker that is replaced each time, initially appealing, but later questioned whether they could rely solely on markers, especially considering similar lazy-loading use cases at Mozilla. Noam Rosenthal and Philip Jägenstedt agreed that options one (using content method with explicit verbs) and four (using a single marker replaced each time) were the strongest contenders. Chris Wilson suggested keeping this topic on the agenda for review after the new year to ensure people have looked at the details and can have a fruitful discussion.
- **Meeting Schedule for Holidays** Chris Wilson proposed canceling the next two meetings due to their falling on Christmas Day and New Year's Day, placing the next meeting on January 8th. There was general agreement.
